title: Chiral Quantum Groups and Holography
subtitle: Local operations, duality and reconstruction
audience: Mathematicians and theoretical physicists entering the programme

chapters.title: Boundary observables and reconstruction
chapters.summary: What boundary observables must retain if they are to determine bulk operations and quantum states.

chapters.title: Algebras, modules and combining systems
chapters.summary: Multiplication composes observables; coproducts combine their actions; associators, braidings and adjunctions specify the resulting comparisons.

chapters.title: Local fields on a curve
chapters.summary: Position-dependent products are defined through fields, modes, translation and their singular expansions; a complete current calculation explains the passage to differential modules.

chapters.title: Factorization and collision geometry
chapters.summary: Configuration opens, diagonal targets and compatible collision extensions define chiral and factorization operations; consecutive cuts explain the different support required by ordered associative duality.

chapters.title: The strongest remaining questions
chapters.summary: Eleven exact comparison problems identify the strongest remaining questions while preserving their established constructions and counterexamples.

figures.title: Finite diagonal tensors and their coordinatewise limit
figures.caption: For V equal to the space of all complex sequences, V ⊗ V consists of finite-rank matrices. The finite diagonals D⁽ᴺ⁾ converge coordinatewise to the infinite identity matrix, which lies in the specified completion and has infinite rank. Every displayed matrix is only a finite viewport.
figures.domain: V = product over n≥0 of C. The algebraic tensor image has the coordinatewise topology inherited from the full matrix product. Its completion is the full product over (i,j)≥0 of C.

figures.title: The two triangle identities of an adjunction
figures.caption: For F left adjoint to G, the unit η and counit ε satisfy two identities. These identities hold for every adjunction. Invertibility of the unit or counit is an additional property, with the consequences stated below.
figures.domain: Categories C and D with an adjunction F:C→D, G:D→C. X belongs to C and Y belongs to D. The chapter writes Φ and Ψ for its particular F and G.

states.label: Triangle at FX
states.meaning: Applying F to the unit and then evaluating by the counit recovers the original object FX.

states.label: Triangle at GY
states.meaning: Applying the unit and then G to the counit recovers the original object GY.

properties.hypothesis: Every component η_X is an isomorphism.
properties.explanation: For every pair X,X′, F induces a bijection on their morphism sets.

properties.hypothesis: Every component ε_Y is an isomorphism.
properties.explanation: For every pair Y,Y′, G induces a bijection on their morphism sets.

properties.hypothesis: Both η and ε are natural isomorphisms.
properties.equivalent_statement: F and G give inverse equivalences of C and D.
properties.explanation: Both comparison maps are invertible on their entire displayed categories.

diagrams.title: The support detected by consecutive cuts
diagrams.caption: For three ordered labels, the complement of the two separating opens is \(Z_3=\Delta_{13}\). The small diagonal lies inside it; a collision of labels 1 and 3 with label 2 elsewhere defeats both cuts.
hypotheses: Smooth curve; external input order 1,2,3; only consecutive cuts.

witness.conclusion: Both consecutive cuts fail, although the point is outside the small diagonal.

diagrams.title: Bar and cobar retain the ordered operations

diagrams.title: From a character to an action, and back to the vacuum
diagrams.caption: The complete spaces retain the pointing homotopy and its higher compatibilities. Multiplication followed by vacuum evaluation gives \(\Psi\Theta\simeq1\). The reverse composite is the recognition question; it is proved on the families stated below and remains open for arbitrary admitted actors.

diagrams.title: The two coproduct paths give the same three-system action
diagrams.caption: The tensor \(\boxtimes_\rho\) includes its cross contraction. The level group need not be commutative. Both paths have the displayed triple value, so coassociativity preserves the order of the levels.
hypotheses: Flat Hopf algebra with bijective antipode over a characteristic-zero coefficient algebra.
Translation, unitary spectral coquasitriangular form and level automorphisms satisfy all displayed identities in Chapter 12.
The fields and all finite products have the specified common rational germs and expansion domains.

diagrams.title: Extension multiplication retains its middle geometry
diagrams.caption: The left map remembers quotient and subobject; the right map remembers the middle object. Pullback along \(p\) followed by the specified pushforward along \(q\) gives the Hall operation. Three-step flags compare its two bracketings.
hypotheses: The constructible-function integral uses finite charge support and an actual domain on which Euler integration is defined.
The coefficient-complex formula is additional data on its specified critical/oriented correspondence; its shifts, supports and orientation roots are retained.
